NOT EVEN GOOD ENOUGH TO PLAY, LET ALONE FINISH

I tried. I really tried — because I absolutely love the original Mass Effect trilogy. The idea behind Andromeda wasn’t the problem; in fact, the core concept had real potential. But the execution turned out painfully disappointing.

Pros:
✅ Dynamic, fast-paced combat that brings a bit of freshness to the formula.
✅ A genuinely interesting narrative idea that I respect a lot — it leaves the trilogy’s endings untouched while opening the door for massive world-building opportunities.
✅ Rare thing for me to say, but the marketing campaign deserves praise. It completely pulled me in.

Cons:
❌ The execution is a disaster. The game looks bad, the worlds feel empty, and the overall design feels several levels below the original trilogy.
❌ Andromeda is hollow. There’s no effort put into creating memorable alien races, meaningful mythology, or a compelling sci-fi identity. It all feels painfully lazy.
❌ The class system feels ruined. I understand the argument for “more freedom,” but the old system had more personality. I would’ve improved it — not rewritten it. (This point is personal preference, but it matters to me.)
❌ The characters are written as if they’re supposed to feel interesting, but aside from the Krogan, they simply don’t. Most of them feel like shallow “woke culture” stereotypes — flat archetypes with no charm, no personality, and nothing memorable to say. Even after patches that tried to fix the now-famous “crazy faces,” everyone still looks ugly, sounds terrible and behave even worse. Playing as a young, inexperienced protagonist only makes me appreciate the seasoned, battle-tested Shepard three times more.
❌ The story is dull, generic, and feels like homework copied from the trilogy without its heart or legacy. This isn’t a space opera — almost nothing actually happens.
❌ The wasted potential hurts the most. The alien threat matters, sure… but I feel the game should’ve leaned far more into the “colonization” theme — environmental hazards, terraforming tech, moral dilemmas, unique survival mechanics. Instead, we get a reheated plotline that once worked, but here falls completely flat. And the Kett? The name alone feels like a weak echo of the Geth — an absolute low point.

For me, this is one of the most wasted opportunities in modern gaming. I’m genuinely heartbroken and can’t recommend it to anyone. What worries me most is how the failure of Andromeda might affect the upcoming Mass Effect 5 — a project that could decide not only the future of this epic series, but possibly the fate of BioWare itself.

NOT RECOMMENDED
